title: Tracking Representations in LLM Reasoning Traces for Iterated Games
abstract: arXiv:2611.23403v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents achieve state-of-the-art performance across domains through chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning. Despite their ubiquitous use, little is understood about the relationship between the externalized trace and the model's actual computation. We address this by investigating how LLM agents make decisions in iterative games with incomplete information. Using a series of mechanistic interpretability techniques, we find that the model forms and iteratively revises an internal representation of the game throughout the CoT. Once the model prematurely commits to an incorrect belief, it rarely recovers. This failure is manifested in both the literal trace and the layer activations. Ultimately, as multi-agent systems are more prevalent, our work opens the door to a more focused diagnosis of their strategic reasoning errors. translated_title: 迭代博弈中LLM推理轨迹的表示追踪
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）智能体通过思维链（CoT）推理在各个领域取得了最先进的性能。尽管其应用无处不在，但人们对外部化的推理轨迹与模型实际计算之间的关系知之甚少。我们通过研究LLM智能体在信息不完整的迭代博弈中如何做出决策来应对这一问题。利用一系列机制可解释性技术，我们发现模型在整个思维链过程中会形成并迭代地修正其对博弈的内部表示。一旦模型过早地陷入错误的信念，它很少能够恢复。这种失败在字面推理轨迹和层间激活中均有体现。随着多智能体系统日益普及，我们的工作为更有针对性地诊断其策略推理错误打开了大门。出于演示目的，我们还提供了该方法在选定场景上的交互式可视化工具。
tldr: 该论文通过机制可解释性技术揭示了LLM在迭代博弈中会在思维链里形成并迭代修正博弈的内部表示，但一旦过早形成错误信念便难以恢复，且这种失败同时体现在推理轨迹和内部激活之中。
en_tdlr: This paper uses mechanistic interpretability to show that LLMs form and iteratively revise internal representations of games during chain-of-thought reasoning, but once they prematurely commit to an incorrect belief they rarely recover—a failure visible in both the reasoning trace and layer activations.
